limitations: One historically curated list with English elicitation labels; neither representative of all concept lists nor independent cross-language observations.
Labels and definitions are comparison aids, not a complete Meaning IR, universal ontology, lexicalization requirement or rule for generating words.
Twelve entries do not prove coverage of user canon, sentence tasks, argument structure, scope, polysemy or pragmatic commitment.
Source-list mappings are curated judgments, preserved as published rather than corrected or treated as ground truth.
This selection is development material, not a sealed audit or evidence for linguistic naturalness.

Only three selected tables and their mapping closure are checked; this is not general CLDF/schema/foreign-key validation. Gloss languages are elicitation-label languages, not target-language doculects.
selection.method: Purposive developer selection by fixed source-entry IDs, covering a few participants, actions, entities and negation for development examples; no random sampling or frequency estimate.
selection.samplingUnit: source-list entry; mapped concept sets are comparison targets, not sampled languages or doculects

conceptlists.csv.Description: Swadesh's most famous concept list of 100 items. The original article lists all 215 items originally proposed in the first article on [lexicostatistics in 1950](sources.bib#cldf:Swadesh1950), but marks the most stable 92 items, and adds eight more items which became then the list of 100 items as shown here. In the list, we marked the eight additional items with an asterisk preceding the concept label. Since this list was only implicitly provided in Swadesh's original publication, we ordered the items alphabetically.
conceptlists.csv.Name: Swadesh, Morris 1955
